scope: Conservative client-side request/subscription state and cleanup contract; offline static evidence only

identity_policy: Keep caller output pointer, transaction pointer, numeric request value, and cyclic-ID object distinct.
Treat returned ID as opaque; preserve exact bits and do not infer allocation, scope, uniqueness, reuse, or cross-instance validity.
Track async requests and cyclic subscriptions independently, even for equal numeric IDs.
If output is absent/unchanged/ambiguous, do not synthesize an ID or remove by a guessed value.
cleanup_policy: Keep pReqID output storage writable and alive while a request may still write through it.
Do not release callback/output resources while in-flight access remains possible.
Treat RemoveCyclicVariables as a removal request, not a proven synchronous drain barrier.
Shutdown: stop new work, request removal of known cyclic items, maintain resources through chosen quiescence, then release; no binary-proven cancellation/drain guarantee.

evidence.claim: Public entrypoint targets/slots for async, cyclic read, and cyclic removal
pReqID pointer stored at transaction +0x98; transaction pointer returned and stored separately in wrapper +0x04
+0x20 scalar passed to RID formatter; producer/output identity and ReqID lookup not established
CCyclicID lifecycle separate from CTransactionID lifecycle
evidence.classification: separate symbols/list machinery; no identity bridge
disassembly; does not prove insertion/quiescence semantics

evidence.claim: Field-use scan is candidate offsets, not semantic ownership

unresolved_transitions: Async submission -> numeric ID producer -> caller output write
Cyclic ID production -> StartCyclics -> list insertion
Cyclic removal -> per-record deletion and callback quiescence
